interfaces.exact_interface_read:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every subgroup $H$ of a finite-dimensional real
Lie group $G$ that is closed as a subset of $G$ has a unique smooth structure
making it an embedded Lie subgroup of $G$.

The countable-choice assumption is required by the currently available local
exponential and BCH interfaces and is used once more to select a sequence in
the local transverse contradiction. No connectedness assumption is made.

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, a finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$, and a subgroup $H\le G$ that is closed in $G$.

[A1] $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is countable choice. [[def-countable-choice]].

[F1] The exponential restricts to a diffeomorphism from a neighborhood of $0\in\mathfrak g$ onto an identity neighborhood in $G$. [[cor-the-exponential-map-is-a-local-diffeomorphism-at-zero]].

[F2] Locally, $\log(\exp X\exp Y)=\operatorname{BCH}(X,Y)$; the BCH series has linear term $X+Y$ and its terms of degree at least two converge uniformly on smaller balls. [[thm-baker-campbell-hausdorff]], [[def-baker-campbell-hausdorff-series]], [[lem-local-convergence-of-the-baker-campbell-hausdorff-series]].

[F3] Along a fixed line, $(\exp Z)^n=\exp(nZ)$ for every integer $n$. [[prop-exponential-scales-one-parameter-subgroups]].

[F4] A finite-dimensional subspace has a linear complement, and a smooth map with invertible differential has a smooth local inverse. [[lem-finite-dimensional-subspace-admits-a-linear-projection-without-choice]], [[thm-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-on-manifolds]].

[F5] A bounded sequence in a finite-dimensional real coordinate space has a convergent subsequence. [[cor-bolzano-weierstrass-in-rn]].

[F6] Slice charts define embedded submanifolds, and the tangent algebra of an immersed Lie subgroup is a Lie subalgebra. [[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]], [[prop-the-lie-algebra-of-a-lie-subgroup-is-a-lie-subalgebra]].

interfaces.exact_interface_read:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

interfaces.exact_interface_read:
Let $V$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space with inner product linear in its first argument. A **finite adiabatic path** is a family $H(s):V\to V$ of linear endomorphisms ([[def-linear-map]]) indexed by $s\in[0,1]$, whose matrix entries are twice continuously differentiable in $s$ and such that $H(s)=H(s)^*$ for every $s\in[0,1]$. A **coherently followed spectral band** is a norm-continuous family of orthogonal projections $P(s):V\to V$ indexed by $s\in[0,1]$, of one fixed rank $m\ge1$, commuting with $H(s)$, whose range is a sum of full eigenspaces and which locally continues the same isolated cluster. For a finite union of positively oriented circles $\Gamma$, define $\oint_\Gamma F(z)\,dz$ as the sum of the parameterized integrals $\int_0^{2\pi}F(c+re^{it})ire^{it}\,dt$ over its circle components. Local continuation means that on each neighborhood there is such a contour enclosing exactly the selected cluster and
$$P(s)=-\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma(H(s)-zI)^{-1}\,dz.$$
With $Q(s)=I-P(s)$, define the **full gap**
$$g(s)=\min\{|\lambda-\mu|:\lambda\in\sigma(H(s)|_{\operatorname{ran}P(s)}),\ \mu\in\sigma(H(s)|_{\operatorname{ran}Q(s)})\}.$$
If $Q(s)=0$, the full gap is $+\infty$. Admissible gapped paths have a uniform full gap $\inf_{s\in[0,1]}g(s)>0$. Distinct eigenvalues inside the band may cross; its total rank remains $m$.

For a real parameter $T\in\mathbb R$, the slow-time propagator $U_T$ is the unique solution of
$$i\frac{d}{ds}U_T(s)=T H(s)U_T(s),\qquad U_T(0)=I.$$
Identifying complex coordinates with real and imaginary parts reduces this to a real finite matrix ODE ([[lem-linear-matrix-odes-have-unique-global-solutions-on-a-given-interval]]); differentiating $U_T(s)^*U_T(s)$ shows it stays unitary.

An instance also supplies an explicit preparation isometry $A_0:\mathbb C^m\to V$ with image $\operatorname{ran}P(0)$ and its declared preparation cost. For a rank-one band this means a specified unit vector $\psi_0\in\operatorname{ran}P(0)$ and a circuit preparing it; for a rank-$m$ band it is an orthonormal frame, not just the matrix $H(0)$ or the projector $P(0)$. Given an input density operator $\rho_{\rm in}$ on $\mathbb C^m$, the evolved output is $\rho_T=U_T(1)A_0\rho_{\rm in}A_0^*U_T(1)^*$. This is a density operator: for $W=U_T(1)A_0$, $W^*W=A_0^*U_T(1)^*U_T(1)A_0=I$ by isometry and unitarity; hence $W\rho_{\rm in}W^*$ is nonnegative by its quadratic form, and $\operatorname{tr}(W\rho_{\rm in}W^*)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{\rm in}W^*W)=1$ by trace cyclicity ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]], [[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). A rank-one input is the pure-state projector ([[def-qc-pure-state-and-ray]], [[def-qc-density-operator]]). A supplied target density operator $\sigma$ on $V$ is compared with $\rho_T$ by trace distance $D(\rho_T,\sigma)$ ([[def-qc-trace-distance]]). A finite output POVM on $V$ and an accepting outcome set may be supplied; its success probability is the sum of the corresponding POVM probabilities ([[def-qc-povm-and-outcome-law]], [[thm-qc-povm-probabilities-normalize]]). A finite projective measurement on $V$ may also be supplied, with success probability given by its projective outcome law ([[def-qc-projective-measurement]], [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]]); this is a special case of the POVM interface. The model is mathematical and includes no physical postulate.

interfaces.exact_interface_read:
Let $H:[0,1]\to\mathcal L(V)$ be a $C^2$ finite-dimensional Hermitian path, and let $P(s)$ be a coherently followed spectral projection of constant rank $m\ge1$, separated from its complement by full gap $g(s)>0$. Let $U_T$ solve $iU_T'(s)=TH(s)U_T(s)$ with $U_T(0)=I$, where $T>0$. Define
$$A_m(s)=\frac1T\left[\frac{m\|H'(0)\|}{g(0)^2}+\frac{m\|H'(s)\|}{g(s)^2}+\int_0^s\left(\frac{m\|H''(r)\|}{g(r)^2}+\frac{7m\sqrt m\|H'(r)\|^2}{g(r)^3}\right)dr\right].$$
Then
$$\|U_T(s)P(0)U_T(s)^*-P(s)\|\le A_m(s).$$
For every unit $\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P(0)$, its transition probability out of the band at time $s$ is at most $A_m(s)^2$. The rank $m$ may be larger than the number of distinct eigenvalues in the band; using rank in the constants is a valid upper bound.

interfaces.exact_interface_read:
Use the Fibonacci fusion rule $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$ and the
fixed-chirality data
$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_\tau=\begin{pmatrix}\phi^{-1}&\phi^{-1/2}\\
\phi^{-1/2}&-\phi^{-1}\end{pmatrix}$ and
$r=R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}$. The fixed-total-charge B6 path bases are

$$\mathcal P_1=\{0101010,0101110,0110110,0111010,0111110\},$$

$$\mathcal P_\tau=\{0101011,0101101,0101111,0110101,0110111,0111011,0111101,0111111\},$$

where each path is $(x_0,\ldots,x_6)$, $x_0=0$ is the unit label,
$x_1=1$ is $\tau$, and adjacent labels obey the fusion rule. For
$d_0=1,d_1=\phi$, define $E_i$ on either path basis by
$$(E_i)_{x,y}= \begin{cases} \sqrt{d_{x_i}d_{y_i}}/d_{x_{i-1}}, &x_j=y_j\ (j\ne i),\ x_{i-1}=x_{i+1}=y_{i-1}=y_{i+1},\\ 0,&\text{otherwise,} \end{cases} \qquad P_i:=\phi^{-1}E_i.$$
Then $P_i$ are orthogonal projections, have ranks $2$ on $\mathcal P_1$
and $3$ on $\mathcal P_\tau$, satisfy
$P_iP_{i+1}P_i=\phi^{-2}P_i$ and commute at separation at least two.
Consequently $B_i=rI+(1-r)P_i$ are unitary matrices satisfying the Artin
relations of $B_6$, with
$\det B_i=r^3$ on $V(\tau^6\to1)$ and $\det B_i=r^5$ on
$V(\tau^6\to\tau)$.

interfaces.exact_interface_read:
Let $r=e^{-3\pi i/5}$, $\phi=(1+\sqrt5)/2=1-r-r^{-1}$, and
$s=\sqrt\phi>0$. Then
$$\mathbb Z[r,s]\cong \mathbb Z[x,y]\big/\bigl(x^4-x^3+x^2-x+1,\ y^2-(1-x-x^{-1})\bigr),$$
where $x^{-1}=x^9$. The assignment
$$r\mapsto15,\qquad r^{-1}\mapsto29,\qquad \phi\mapsto19,\qquad s\mapsto9$$
defines a ring homomorphism to $\mathbb F_{31}$. The elements $r$ and
$\phi$ map to nonzero units, and conjugation of coefficients is handled by
$r\mapsto r^{-1}$ before reduction.

interfaces.exact_interface_read:
Take the skeletal complex-linear category whose simple labels are
$\mathbf1,\tau$ and whose objects are finite direct sums of them, including
the empty direct sum $0$. For objects
$A=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus m_s}$ and $B=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus n_s}$, set
$\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=\bigoplus_s\operatorname{Mat}_{n_s\times m_s}(\mathbb C)$;
composition is block-matrix multiplication, dagger is conjugate transpose,
and the norm is the maximum of the operator norms of its blocks. Thus direct
sums are orthogonal. Define tensor product on simple labels by the fusion rules
$\mathbf1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf1=a$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$,
and extend it distributively to direct sums. For each allowed simple fusion
channel $c\subset a\otimes b$, let $i_{ab}^c:c\to a\otimes b$ be the
standard unit-vector isometric inclusion. Since the multiplicity space is
$V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$, its orthonormal basis vector is
the adjoint projection $(i_{ab}^c)^\dagger:a\otimes b\to c$; retain
$i_{ab}^c$ itself for the coevaluation construction below. On simple-label
blocks, tensor a pair
of morphism matrices by their Kronecker product on multiplicity coordinates
and by the identity on each simple fusion channel; extend over direct sums.
This defines a bifunctor compatible with dagger. Use the strict unit gauge:
every F or R coordinate involving $\mathbf1$ is the identity. Put

$$\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad u=\phi^{-1},\qquad v=\phi^{-1/2}.$$

The only nontrivial associator blocks are

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=[1],\qquad F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix},$$

in the intermediate-channel order $(\mathbf1,\tau)$. In the pullback R
convention of [[def-qc-tqc-r-symbol]], the exchange blocks are

$$R^{\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=x=e^{-4\pi i/5},\qquad R^{\tau\tau}_{\tau}=y=e^{3\pi i/5}.$$

Because these are pullback symbols, define the object-level braiding
$c_{\tau,\tau}$ on the $\mathbf1$ and $\tau$ summands by $x^{-1}$ and
$y^{-1}$, respectively. Every braiding with a unit input is the strict
identity. These fixed chiral data define the Fibonacci unitary braided fusion
category in this gauge; the verification checks every nontrivial pentagon and
hexagon sector.

interfaces.exact_interface_read:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary fusion category and fix a set
$\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$ of representatives for the simple
isomorphism classes. Throughout this definition, the ordered input charges
$a_1,\ldots,a_n$, total charge $d$, and all internal edge charges are labels
in $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$. Also fix a parenthesized binary fusion
tree. At each internal vertex with incoming charges $x,y$ and outgoing charge
$z$, choose one vector from an orthonormal basis of $V_{xy}^z$. An
**admissible labeling** assigns a representative charge to each internal edge
so that each chosen vertex basis is nonempty; a separate multiplicity-basis
index is retained at every vertex. Compose the vertex morphisms, inserting the
associators required by the chosen tree, to obtain a morphism from the
parenthesized input tensor to $d$. These composite morphisms are the
**fusion-tree vectors**. The family is called a **fusion-tree basis** when it
is an orthonormal basis of the fixed-input, fixed-total fusion space. For the
empty input list the tensor is $\mathbf1$ and its empty tree vector is
$\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf1}$ when $d=\mathbf1$; for one input $a_1$, the
only tree vector is $\operatorname{id}_{a_1}$ when $d=a_1$. The next local
lemma proves the basis property for every finite input list and includes the
dimension recursion ([[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]]).

interfaces.exact_interface_read:
Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. Put

$$\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)=\{x\in\mathrm{TL}_n:\tau_n(xy)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathrm{TL}_n\}.$$

Let $I_n$ be the two-sided ideal generated by $p_{\ell-1}\otimes1_{n-\ell+1}$ for $n\ge\ell-1$, and $I_n=0$ below that rank. Then $I_n=\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)$, and $\mathrm{TL}_n/I_n$ is the direct sum of full matrix algebras with multiplicities given by length-$n$ paths from $0$ of heights $0,\ldots,\ell-2$. The additive idempotent-complete negligible quotient has simple labels $0,\ldots,\ell-2$, represented by $p_a$, and

$$a\otimes b\cong\bigoplus_{\substack{|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b)\\c\equiv a+b\ (2)}}c.$$

At $n=\ell-1$ the unreduced algebra is semisimple, while its trace radical is the nonzero one-dimensional block generated by $p_{\ell-1}$. Trace radical and Jacobson radical are therefore distinct at this first boundary.
